definition.def: If you imply that something is the case, you say something which indicates that it is the case in an indirect way.
examples: 'Are you implying that I have something to do with those attacks?' she asked coldly. [VERB that]
She felt undermined by the implied criticism. [VERB-ed]

definition.def: If an event or situation implies that something is the case, it makes you think it likely that it is the case.
examples: Exports in June rose 1.5%, implying that the economy was stronger than many investors thought. [VERB that]
A high fat intake nearly always implies a low fibre intake. [VERB noun]

examples.sentence: A still picture could only imply the existence of time, while time in a novel passed at the whim of the reader.
This would imply the relationships are only superficial.
